# Innovation Architecture Rules

<!-- Generated by packages/rules/generate.mjs from data/laws/*.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

The tactics come from public product-discovery and experimentation practice: customer interviews, assumption mapping, smoke tests, service prototypes, pre-commitments, and the innovation-accounting metrics that decide whether any of them was worth running. Each card states a hypothesis with the threshold it pre-commits to, the method (time, cost, confidence), the three stages that run it, and the named false positive that makes that particular test lie.
The hypothesis prints on the card exactly as the source states it, threshold included, because an experiment without its validation criterion is an opinion. The three stages print compressed to one line each; the full stages, the full warning and the method values follow here, because this file is the reference.

## Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics

### I30 — Refundable Deposit Pre-Order

**Hypothesis and threshold.** We believe users will pay [Price Y] for our forthcoming product. We will verify this by running a pre-order campaign with a required, refundable $50 reservation deposit, and consider it validated if ≥ 3.0% of unique page visitors complete the checkout transaction.

**Schematic.** Payment at step 2 of the 3-step strip

**Method.** Time: 7–14 days · Cost: $100–$500 · Confidence: Extreme (Financial commitment)

**Plan.**
- Preparation: State the product is in development and offer priority queue placement for a refundable deposit.
- Execution: Drive qualified traffic to the reservation page and process real payments via a gateway.
- Data collection: Measure payment completion, refunds requested, and checkout questions.

**False positive.** Frictionless Refund Psychology

When deposits are low and refundable, buyers treat checkout as a bookmark rather than a commitment.

**Plan as written.**
- Preparation: Build a checkout flow that clearly states the product is in active development, offering priority queue placement in exchange for a refundable deposit.
- Execution: Drive qualified traffic to the reservation page and process real financial transactions via a payment gateway.
- Data collection: Measure payment completion rates, refund requests, and customer questions submitted during checkout.

**Warning as written.** When deposits are low, fully refundable, and clearly framed as risk-free, conversion rates often artificially inflate, as buyers treat the checkout as an easy way to bookmark the product rather than an actual purchase commitment.

**Source.** The source names no originator.

## Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics

### I37 — Unit Economics Stress Test (CAC:LTV Ratio)

**Hypothesis and threshold.** We believe our customer acquisition model is economically sustainable. We will verify this by measuring blended and paid Customer Acquisition Costs alongside early cohort churn and revenue, and consider it validated if the projected Lifetime Value to Customer Acquisition Cost ratio exceeds 3:1, with full CAC payback achieved in ≤ 12 months: frac{text{LTV}}{text{CAC}} ≥ 3.0 quad text{where} quad text{LTV} = frac{text{ARPU} × text{Gross Margin}}{text{Churn Rate}}

**Schematic.** Read at step 3 of the 3-step strip

**Method.** Time: 30–60 days · Cost: $500–$$$$ · Confidence: High

**Plan.**
- Preparation: Aggregate fully loaded acquisition costs across a 60-day window: spend, commissions, overhead, tools.
- Execution: Track paid customer accounts generated specifically from those spend allocations.
- Data collection: Calculate CAC payback months and the projected LTV to CAC ratio.

**False positive.** Blended CAC Smuggling

Blending organic traffic with paid spend hides high paid acquisition costs and an unviable channel.

**Plan as written.**
- Preparation: Aggregate all fully loaded acquisition costs (ad spend, sales commissions, operational overhead, marketing software) across a 60-day testing window.
- Execution: Track the total number of paid customer accounts generated specifically from those spend allocations.
- Data collection: Calculate the months required to recover customer acquisition costs: text{Payback Period (Months)} = frac{text{CAC}}{text{ARPU} × text{Gross Margin %}}

**Warning as written.** Blending cheap organic, direct, or personal network traffic with paid marketing spend obscures high paid customer acquisition costs, hiding an unviable acquisition channel.

**Source.** The source names no originator.

### I39 — Micro-Conversion Step Drop-Off Audit

**Hypothesis and threshold.** We believe that [Step 3 in our onboarding flow] causes unnecessary user drop-off. We will verify this by instrumenting telemetry across every form field and screen transition, and consider it validated if simplifying that single step reduces drop-off by ≥ 30% without lowering downstream activation quality.

**Schematic.** Read at step 3 of the 3-step strip

**Method.** Time: 7–14 days · Cost: $0 · Confidence: High

**Plan.**
- Preparation: Map every field, click and screen transition in the target path into a sequential funnel.
- Execution: Log drop-off, validation errors and interaction times across 500 sessions.
- Data collection: Plot the drop-off gradient across each micro-step to find friction.

**False positive.** Removing Essential Friction

Cutting identity checks or qualification questions raises completion and floods the product with junk accounts.

**Plan as written.**
- Preparation: Map every user input field, click, and screen transition in the target path into a sequential funnel model.
- Execution: Log drop-off percentages, validation errors, and interaction times for every field across 500 user sessions.
- Data collection: Plot the drop-off gradient across each micro-step to identify points of user friction.

**Warning as written.** Streamlining onboarding forms by cutting out identity checks or qualification questions can boost completion rates while flooding the product with unqualified or spam accounts.

**Source.** The source names no originator.
